explanation: I found no single Mathlib declaration that states this identity or specializes to it. The statement is t^(-5/2) · (√(3t))^5 = 3^(5/2) for t > 0, a concrete calculation. Proving it takes several separate Mathlib facts: `Real.rpow_div_two_eq_sqrt` and `Real.rpow_natCast` to rewrite √(3t)^5 as (3t)^(5/2), `Real.mul_rpow` to split (3t)^(5/2) into 3^(5/2) · t^(5/2), and `Real.rpow_neg` with `inv_mul_cancel₀` to cancel the powers of t. That combination is more than the one-or-two-line instantiation of a single declaration that would count as a special case. I did not run any searches. I gave this verdict from the structure of the proof, because a concrete identity like this is unlikely to appear in Mathlib as its own lemma.
